_readme: JS-side (WP4) edge cases for reward engine v2 (plan C3/C5). Both engines load this file.
Expected values are derived by hand from C3; each scenario says why in `why`.
All data is synthetic: card, merchant and VPA names are test values, not real accounts.
The top-level directory replaces db/fixtures/merchant_directory.json for this file.

scenarios.name: J01 MCC include matches
scenarios.why: mcc 5411 is in the rule set: 10 blocks x 5 = 50 points (base 10 + bonus 40).

scenarios.name: J02 info rule is never ranked
scenarios.why: p-info has the lowest priority and no restriction, but info never applies; nothing else does, so the implicit base pays 10.

scenarios.name: J03 unknown MCC: category stands in
scenarios.why: mcc unknown but the rule also names cat-dining, which matches: 3 x 10 = 30 points.

scenarios.name: J04 known MCC outside the set fails despite the category
scenarios.why: mcc 5999 is known and not 5812/5814, so the category cannot stand in; implicit base.

scenarios.name: J05 MCC-only exclusion rule
scenarios.why: mcc 6540 matches the exclusion rule: nothing earned, rule_id is the exclusion.

scenarios.name: J06 mcc_exclude switches an earn rule off
scenarios.why: Online rule excludes mcc 4900; implicit base pays 10.

scenarios.name: J07 priority tie goes to the higher pre-cap value
scenarios.why: Both rules are priority 10; online 5% (₹50) beats shopping 3% (₹30) on this transaction (D12c).

scenarios.name: J08 VPA prefix wins over the name
scenarios.why: Name says Swiggy, VPA user part starts with "zomato": Zomato 7%.

scenarios.name: J09 VPA prefix is a starts-with match
scenarios.why: "swiggyfood" starts with the prefix "swiggy": Swiggy 10%.

scenarios.name: J10 parent does not match a sub-brand-only rule
scenarios.why: Swiggy resolves to swiggy; the Instamart-only rule needs instamart. Swiggy 10% applies.

scenarios.name: J11 longest alias picks the sub-brand
scenarios.why: "swiggy instamart" beats "swiggy"; Instamart 6% (priority 5) beats the parent Swiggy rule (priority 10).

scenarios.name: J12 caller-supplied merchant_slug wins
scenarios.why: merchant_slug zomato is used as given; the name resolves to nothing.

scenarios.name: J13 unknown merchant falls to the base rule
scenarios.why: No alias matches; the explicit base rule pays 1%.

scenarios.name: J14 rule inside its validity window
scenarios.why: The festive rule runs 1-31 Oct; mid-October it pays 15%.

scenarios.name: J15 block_inr overrides the unit block
scenarios.why: 5 pts per ₹150: floor(1000/150) = 6 blocks = 30 points; base 10 on ₹100 blocks; value at ₹0.50.

scenarios.name: J16 platform not in the set
scenarios.why: PhonePe is not SmartBuy; implicit base pays floor(1000/100) x 1.

scenarios.name: J17 round half-up
scenarios.why: ₹300 / ₹200 = 1.5 blocks, rounded half-up to 2; base 2 pts per block = 4 points.

scenarios.name: J18 round half-up on a bonus rule
scenarios.why: ₹500 / ₹200 = 2.5 -> 3 blocks: 18 points (base 6 + bonus 12).

scenarios.name: J19 no rounding keeps fractional blocks
scenarios.why: ₹250 = 2.5 blocks x 3 = 7.5 points at ₹0.20.

scenarios.name: J20 accrual_rounding alone makes a card v2
scenarios.why: No rule_role or cap_kind, but accrual_rounding is set, so unknown rail no longer satisfies the online rule (v1 would pay 5%).

scenarios.name: J21 spend above max_txn earns the base rate
scenarios.why: ₹5,000 at 5 pts/₹100 = 250; the other ₹3,000 at base = 30; 280 points.

scenarios.name: J22 txn-count cap with room consumes one
scenarios.why: One of two counted transactions left: 10% applies and the count cap consumes 1.

scenarios.name: J23 txn-count cap exhausted falls to base
scenarios.why: Count used up: the whole spend is overflow at the 1% base; the count cap consumes 0.

scenarios.name: J24 custom post-cap rate
scenarios.why: ₹500 of spend headroom at 6% = 30; ₹1,000 overflow at the custom 2% = 20.

scenarios.name: J25 parent bonus cap binds inside the child
scenarios.why: Bonus 180; child has 900 left but the parent only 50: base 20 + bonus 50; both consume 50.

scenarios.name: J26 legacy reward_value cap on a points rule
scenarios.why: cap_kind null, ₹25 at ₹0.25/pt = a 100-point total cap: 200 earned, 100 allowed.

scenarios.name: J27 card-wide total cap applies to the implicit base
scenarios.why: No rule applies; 1% base = ₹10, but the card-wide cap has ₹5 left.

scenarios.name: J28 bonus cashback cap keeps the base
scenarios.why: 5% = 50: base 10 + bonus 40, bonus cap has 20 left -> 30; the card-wide total counts 30.

scenarios.name: J29 rule-level excluded category
scenarios.why: The online rule excludes wallet loads; the implicit base pays 1% and counts to the card-wide cap.

scenarios.name: J30 flat points once per transaction
scenarios.why: Flat 500 points (C3.5) against a base of 60 on ₹6,000: bonus 440, so 500 points in all.

scenarios.name: J31 points_half_up applies to the base accrual too
scenarios.why: Rule 7,500 x 3% = 225; base 7,500 x 1.5% = 112.5 -> 113 (D7); bonus 112, but only 100 left in the bonus cap: 213.

card.name: Js Points Half Up Bonus Card

scenarios.name: J32 points_floor on a bonus rule
scenarios.why: 199 x 5% = 9.95 -> 9 on the whole product (per-block floor would give 5); base 2.985 -> 2; bonus 7.

scenarios.name: K01 legacy merchant_pattern on a v2 rule still matches
scenarios.why: D9(2): no merchant_slugs, so the v1 substring "amazon" restricts the rule; "AMAZON PAY INDIA" contains it: 5%.

scenarios.name: K02 legacy merchant_pattern on a v2 rule never widens
scenarios.why: D9(2): any other merchant fails the pattern; the base rule pays 1%.

scenarios.name: K03 derived post-cap behaviour: post_cap_rate 0 means zero
scenarios.why: D9(3): behaviour null + post_cap_rate 0 -> zero. ₹500 headroom at 5% = 25; the other ₹500 earns nothing.

scenarios.name: K04 derived post-cap behaviour: another rate means custom_rate
scenarios.why: D9(3): behaviour null + post_cap_rate 2 -> custom 2% in the rule unit: 25 + ₹500 x 2% = 35.

scenarios.name: K05 cross-currency rule: each cap binds its own currency
scenarios.why: D9(5)/(7): ₹600 at 5% cashback = ₹30, all bonus (base is points); bonus-cashback cap leaves ₹20. Above-max ₹400 earns 4 base points; the points total cap leaves 2. Value 2 x 0.25 + 20.

scenarios.name: K06 equally binding eligible-spend caps: first in catalogue order wins
scenarios.why: D9(8): both caps have ₹500 left; et-cap-a (first, zero) binds, so the ₹500 overflow earns nothing. Both consume 500; the count cap takes 1.

scenarios.name: K07 count cap takes 1 even when a spend cap is exhausted
scenarios.why: D9(8): et-cap-b has nothing left and binds (base_rate): all ₹1,000 earns the 1% base; the count cap still takes 1.

scenarios.name: K08 legacy category cap applies to the implicit base
scenarios.why: D9(9): no rule applies to bills; the 1% base = ₹10 meets a legacy reward_value cap on cat-bills (₹3 total cashback).

scenarios.name: K09 inactive merchant is never resolved
scenarios.why: D9(10): "legacy brand" belongs to an inactive merchant, so nothing resolves and the legacy-brand rule fails; base 1%.

scenarios.name: K10 inactive merchant still counts as an ancestor
scenarios.why: D9(10): "LEGACY BRAND STORE" resolves to the active child, whose parent is the inactive legacy_brand: 8%.

scenarios.name: K11 equal-length VPA prefix tie goes to the slug sorting first
scenarios.why: D9(10): beta_pay and alpha_pay both own "quickpay"; alpha_pay sorts first: 4%.

scenarios.name: K12 custom_rate overflow uses the rule unit and its block_inr
scenarios.why: D12b: ₹600 headroom = 4 x ₹150 blocks x 5 = 20 (base 6 + bonus 14); ₹900 overflow = 6 x ₹150 blocks x 2 = 12; 32 points at ₹0.50.

scenarios.name: K13 priority tie compares this transaction's value: flat points win
scenarios.why: D12c: flat 100 points = ₹25 beats 2 pts/₹100 on ₹2,000 = 40 points = ₹10. 100 points (base 20 + bonus 80).

scenarios.name: K14 a remaining tie goes to the rule id sorting first
scenarios.why: D12c: zz-online and aa-shopping are both priority 20 and both pay 30 points; aa-shopping sorts first.

scenarios.name: K15 unenforceable caps are skipped, never guessed
scenarios.why: D12d: unknown kind, null amount, unknown behaviour and unknown scope are all skipped; only the card total (50 left) binds 100 points.
